obligations.note: PR-1322 names CHG-25126, a standard ticket approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-02, before the change opened and before review. Its component mortgage.cases covers the only touched path, CaseService.java.

Code review approved by wen.li@fernbrook.example (Wen Li, change_approver for baseline-mortgage). Wen Li is a different person from the author Declan Farrell under all of the author's listed addresses.
The approval names head commit b619ce5, which is the change's only commit, so no later commits exist to void it.

records/ci/run.json is a successful run of the full baseline-mortgage suite on head b619ce5: 124 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. The registered control tests for the touched obligations (AuditControlTest#sampledOperationsAreAudited, LoggingControlTest#sampledFlowsDoNotLogNpi) are present and pass, though both are labelled sample. I couldn't re-run the suite locally because the JUnit jar is missing.

The change adds a new state-changing operation (reopen) in AUD-1's scope. The code calls audit.record(actor, EDIT_CASE, caseId, "reopened"), which captures actor, action, target and time. But AUD-1 requires exhaustive evidence, its only control test is a sample that never calls reopen, and no new test was added despite the PR claim.

The change adds a log call site, log.info("Case " + caseId + " reopened by " + actor.userId()), which by inspection carries no NPI. But LOG-1 requires exhaustive evidence, and its only control test is a sample whose flows don't include reopen, so nothing tests the new call site.

summary: The change adds CaseService.reopen. Its process records are in order: an approved ticket covering mortgage.cases, an independent change_approver review on the final commit, and a green full-suite CI run on that commit. It touches AUD-1 (a new state-changing operation) and LOG-1 (a new log call site). Both require exhaustive evidence, but their only control tests are sample tests that don't exercise reopen, and the claimed unit-test update doesn't exist. The code looks compliant on inspection, but the evidence isn't adequate to establish either obligation, so the decision is HOLD pending tests that cover reopen. Separately, a reopened case whose NPI was already purged keeps its purge marker, so Retention would never purge NPI entered after a reopen-and-withdraw cycle. That RET-1 risk should be addressed even though RET-1's scoped files were not changed.
